name: Waltz
notes: Slow Waltz style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). The gateway ballroom dance, with its history told whole: the waltz descends from the Austrian-German Ländler, and when its rotating CLOSE HOLD reached polite society in the 1810s it was a genuine scandal — condemned from pulpits and papers as indecent, then danced by everyone anyway (every 'shocking' dance in this app stands in that lineage; the waltz was first). The Viennese original spins fast; the SLOW (English) waltz this pack teaches was codified in 1920s London — Victor Silvester and the ISTD's English style set the box, the rise and fall, and the syllabus that studios worldwide still teach. Design truths: the box step is genuinely solo-trainable and is ballroom's shared alphabet; RISE AND FALL is the soul (down on 1, rising through 2, up on 3, sinking to begin again — breath made visible); the frame is prepped solo; the partnered whisk-and-chassé world is 🤝 late — ballroom studios are famously structured, welcoming, and everywhere. The 3/4 waltz pattern has been in this app's Rhythm Trainer since the ballet pack.

seasons.finale: Film yourself counting and swaying ONE-two-three through a full waltz — the downbeat owned, the lilt found.
Film the box step both directions — six counts, closed feet, clean corners — for one full song.
Film the box with rise and fall breathing through it — down on 1, up through 3, sinking to restart. The soul, visible.
Film the box danced in frame — arms carried, topline long, the shape a partner would step into.
Take a beginner ballroom class or social — studios run them constantly, and the waltz is always the first door.

attributes.name: Downbeat ear L1
attributes.test: clap only the ONE through a full waltz — the bar's anchor, never lost

attributes.name: Rise-and-fall ankles L1
attributes.test: 20 slow controlled rises through the balls of the feet and soft descents, knees easing — the waltz breathes on these

attributes.name: Topline L1
attributes.test: 60s of tall carriage with arms held in frame position, shoulders down — the topline is ballroom's signature

nodes.name: The three — ONE-two-three
checkpoints: the waltz lives in 3/4: a strong ONE and two lighter steps — the pattern has been in this app's Rhythm Trainer since the ballet pack (the vals of tango nights uses it too)
slow waltz sits near 28-30 bars per minute — unhurried enough to breathe with
hear the bar as one breath: down (1), rising (2), up (3), and sink into the next

nodes.name: Phrasing the song
checkpoints: waltz songs phrase in groups of bars — the box's six counts spread across two bars, and figures land on phrase starts
modern playlists waltz everything from Chopin to film scores to pop in 3/4; the count doesn't care about the century
dance one song counting aloud, one song silent — the second is the real test

nodes.name: The scandal of the close hold
checkpoints: the waltz descends from the Austrian-German Ländler; when its rotating CLOSE HOLD reached ballrooms in the 1810s it was condemned as indecent — papers and pulpits raged, and everyone danced it anyway
every 'scandalous' dance in this app — tango, lambada, perreo — stands in a lineage the waltz opened
two centuries later it is the establishment; remember it was once the rebellion

nodes.name: The English style — Silvester and the syllabus
checkpoints: the SLOW waltz was codified in 1920s London — Victor Silvester (champion, bandleader, author) and the ISTD's English style set the technique studios still teach
International Standard and American Smooth are the two modern branches — same waltz heart, different rules about leaving the frame
the syllabus system (bronze-silver-gold) is ballroom's gift to beginners: a clear ladder, taught everywhere

nodes.name: The waltz sway
checkpoints: weight transfers side to side, one bar per side — settling on the ONE, floating through two-three
tall and unhurried; the waltz never rushes anywhere
this idle sway is where rise and fall will live — build it calm
mistakes: equal weight on all three counts (the ONE is home; the others visit)

nodes.name: The box step
nodes.anchor: ballroom's shared alphabet — six counts, learnable today
checkpoints: forward-side-close, back-side-close — six counts drawing a box on the floor
feet CLOSE fully on 3 and 6 — the close is the figure's signature, never skipped
both starting feet (a partner dances the mirror; own both halves)
small and exact: the box is a discipline before it is a journey
mistakes: drifting the box across the room (it stays home until the traveling figures ask)
skipping the closes (that's a wander, not a waltz)

nodes.name: Rise & fall — the soul
checkpoints: down on 1 (knees ease as the step lands), rising through 2 (up through the ankles), up on 3 (the close floats), sinking to begin again
the wave is continuous — no steps, no shelves, one breath per bar
the contemporary pack's breath work and the buchaechum's vertical breath are cousins; ballroom just formalized it
film from the side: the head should draw a gentle swell, never a staircase
mistakes: popping up on 2 like an elevator (the rise is a curve)
forgetting to come DOWN (fall is half the name)

nodes.name: The frame & topline (solo prep)
checkpoints: the closed frame carried solo: arms curved and held, elbows buoyant, the topline long from hip to head
the frame must survive the rise and fall — breathing below, still above
dance the full box in frame; when it feels like carrying a picture frame through a swell, it's right

nodes.name: The closed hold (with a partner)
checkpoints: the scandalous hold itself, two centuries on: learned at studios and beginner socials, where the waltz has always been the first lesson
the couple shares one rise and fall — that shared breath is the whole partnership
line of dance flows counterclockwise (the two-step and polka packs' river; ballroom wrote the rule)

nodes.name: One waltz, breathing — filmed
checkpoints: one full song: the box in frame, rise and fall continuous, phrases honored
side-angle film for the swell, front-angle for the topline — both must pass
the test is serenity: a waltz that looks like effort isn't one yet

nodes.name: The studio night
checkpoints: find a beginner ballroom class or social — studios run group classes constantly and partner rotation is standard
your box, frame and rise-and-fall are the complete entry kit; the studio adds the couple
one waltz danced with a stranger, both of you breathing the same bar — that's two centuries of scandal, domesticated into joy
